clue.text: Night vision ?

parts.note: the phrase suggests seeing in the dark, but it means something seen while asleep at night

explanation.definitionFit: What the sleeper sees at night is a vision in sleep, the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Invest, put on diamonds, say, for evening wear

indicators.note: the clothing word is set on top of the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: to invest is to clothe, as in robes of office
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Wear diamonds with your formal clothes for an evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal evening clothes for men, tails and the like, are a set of this kind.

clue.text: System of morals badly-hit in City district

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the postal district

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: the word hit is done badly, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Business ethics have taken a beating in the Square Mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' muddles the three letters, and 'in' puts them inside the postcode; the City is London's financial district, the Square Mile.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles governing conduct.

clue.text: Souvenir tome out about human beings

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap around the people
the word tome is put out of order

parts.note: men means people generally

explanation.surface: A keepsake book about people, now out of print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' muddles the book's letters into a new order, and 'about' wraps them round the people, splitting the scrambled word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept to remember a person or event.

clue.text: Flier attacked nursery clothes-hanger

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence a bird swoops on the maid hanging out the washing and pecks off her nose

explanation.surface: A bird dive-bombed someone pegging out the washing in a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery here is a nursery rhyme: in Sing a Song of Sixpence the maid in the garden hanging out the clothes has her nose pecked off by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of the rhyme, baked in a pie with its fellows, is this dark songbird.

clue.text: James of Quality Street

parts.note: the Scottish playwright James Matthew, author of Peter Pan and the comedy Quality Street

explanation.surface: A man called James who lives on a posh street.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. was the Scottish dramatist whose 1901 play gave its title to the chocolate brand.

clue.text: Assign to brew local tea

indicators.note: the two words are brewed up, stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Get someone to make a pot of the regional tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'brew' shuffles LOCAL TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to allot or set aside for a purpose.

clue.text: Minks with an unusual blood connexion

indicators.note: the letters combined are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Minks sharing an odd bloodline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges MINKS AN; 'connexion' is an old spelling of connection, here a person related to you.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male relative, someone related by blood.

clue.text: Descriptive of a sincere flatterer

parts.note: the proverb says copying is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.surface: A portrait of an honest admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: Since copying is the sincerest flattery, the sincere flatterer is one given to copying.

clue.text: Boring publicity for wood spirit

parts.note: dry means dull, tedious
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: Dull advertising for a woodland ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a nymph living in a tree.

clue.text: Here today and gone tomorrow

parts.note: the stock phrase for anything fleeting or short-lived

explanation.definitionFit: Something that lasts only a day or so is transient, the meaning of the word.

clue.text: " Oh, —— bells, be dumb ;" (Housman)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from A. E. Housman's poem Bredon Hill in A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: A poet begs church bells to fall silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks the missing word of Housman's line in Bredon Hill, where the speaker asks the loud wedding bells to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells the poet wants hushed are loud and clamorous ones, filling the gap in the line.

clue.text: Deputy " drest in a little brief authority "?

definitions.meaning: a deputy is the officer next below the chief

definitions.text: " drest in a little brief authority "?
definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's phrase from Measure for Measure, read whimsically as holding command for a short while, as a stand-in does

explanation.surface: A deputy is clothed, as Shakespeare said, in a little brief authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Measure for Measure ('man, proud man, drest in a little brief authority'); a deputy's power is borrowed and temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the officer ranked immediately below the leader, taking charge in their absence.

clue.text: Outcome trying to bring down a high-flier

definitions.text: trying to bring down a high-flier
definitions.meaning: firing upward at a bird in flight, read as a shot aimed up

explanation.surface: The result of an attempt to shoot down a soaring bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcome is a synonym for the end result; a shot fired skyward at a flying bird is the second sense.

clue.text: Where even stay-at-homes may take flight

definitions.text: Where even stay-at-homes may take flight

parts.words: Where even stay-at-homes may take flight
parts.note: a flight here is a set of steps inside the house, not an air journey

explanation.surface: Somewhere even homebodies might travel by air.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is part of every two-storey house, so it is climbed without leaving home.

clue.text: Position of Oliver's mate before sound of the bell

indicators.note: the comedian's name is placed in front of the bell's sound

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stan Laurel
ding is the noise a bell makes

explanation.surface: Where a comedian's partner stood before the bell rang.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were the famous film double act; Oliver Hardy's partner was Stan.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing is a rank or status, a position in a league table or society.

clue.text: Difference between driver and driven in a car

definitions.text: Difference between driver and driven in a car

parts.words: Difference between driver and driven in a car
parts.note: driver and driven are the toothed wheels of a gearbox, not the chauffeur and passenger

explanation.surface: What separates the chauffeur from the passenger in a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: The relation of turns of a driving cog to those of the driven cog is a transmission measure.

clue.text: A secret communicator

parts.note: someone who passes on private matters in trust, rather than a spy

explanation.definitionFit: One who tells another private matters in confidence is a person who confides.

clue.text: A hospital, leg-pull?

parts.note: a leg-pull usually means a joke, but here a hospital literally pulls a broken leg with weights

explanation.surface: A practical joke played in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients with fractures have the limb stretched by weights and pulleys, a medical treatment named after pulling.

clue.text: Towers of fighting craft

parts.note: the armoured gun housings on warships and tanks, not towers of martial skill

explanation.surface: Castle towers that teach the art of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolving armoured gun housings on warships or tanks are named after small towers.

clue.text: North American Indian or Roman philosopher

definitions.meaning: a member of one of the Iroquois nations of New York State
the Stoic writer and tutor to the emperor Nero

explanation.surface: A Native American or a classical thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to an Iroquois people and to the Stoic author of moral letters in Nero's Rome.

clue.text: Sound receiver makes a murder possible

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are rearranged into a possible new word

explanation.surface: A listening device enables an assassination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges A MURDER; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane of the middle ear vibrates to pick up noises, so it is the body's listening part.

clue.text: Hood on board ship looks threatening

indicators.note: the hood is taken on board, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: HMS Hood, the battleship, looks menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' suggests the famous battleship, but it is a cowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown angrily, which is to glower.

clue.text: Warship needs many pilots

parts.note: a large naval vessel that requires lots of pilots because it carries planes, not because it is hard to steer

explanation.surface: A big naval ship requires many pilots to guide it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped naval vessel serving as a floating airfield carries a whole wing of flyers.

clue.text: Like a humble dwelling of course

parts.note: as means in the manner of
a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: Naturally, like a modest cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but 'course' is the definition: the racecourse in Berkshire famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse hosting the royal meeting each June.

clue.text: Could be Gold Brick that got in first

definitions.note: a gold brick is an example of the answer, as could be signals

indicators.note: the small word comes first, ahead of the other

explanation.surface: A swindle that someone managed to pull off before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: A gold brick is also a swindle; here it is a literal bar of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold bar cast in a block is a bullion bar of this name.

clue.text: Ton-up plane ?

parts.note: an aircraft doing a hundred, but read as an old wooden box that can be loaded up with a ton

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an old rickety aeroplane, also a wooden box for goods that might be loaded with a ton.

clue.text: Out-and-out trend of unlucky graph-man's shares

definitions.meaning: a chart of falling share prices runs lower as it moves to the right

explanation.surface: A total slump in a chartist's stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Graphs plot time left to right, so a share price that keeps falling heads down and to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means utter or absolute; a falling line on a chart heads lower as it goes rightward.

clue.text: Prizes, for good cooks ?

definitions.meaning: an excellent cook or housekeeper is affectionately called a gem of the household

explanation.surface: Awards handed out for good cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize is to cherish or value; a valued domestic helper is fondly called a jewel of that name.

clue.text: Bowling goes back to feature under-arms

definitions.note: a heraldic saying sits on a scroll beneath a coat of arms

indicators.note: the sailor's first name is read from right to left

parts.note: Tom Bowling is the sailor of Charles Dibdin's sea song

explanation.surface: Bowling returns to underarm deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowling' looks like cricket but is the sailor Tom Bowling of Dibdin's song; 'goes back' turns TOM to MOT. 'Under-arms' is not underarm bowling but beneath a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic motto is the phrase on a scroll placed below a family's coat of arms.
